official.description_text:
Postdoc in gears - manufacturing to performance
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Industrial Engineering and Management
Job description
We are looking for a postdoctoral researcher in machine elements and production development, with a focus on how manufacturing methods and manufacturing variations affect gear performance. The project is interdisciplinary and is carried out in collaboration across research areas including mechanical design, materials engineering, lightweight design, and production development. You will plan and conduct experimental studies using an FZG test rig, characterize gear geometry and surface properties, and investigate how these affect efficiency, wear, and service life. The project also includes alternative gear materials and manufacturing methods, such as powder metallurgical gears, as well as new lubrication strategies, such as grease lubrication in precision applications. A particular focus is on understanding how variations in geometry and surface properties affect gear function, and how high efficiency can be balanced against long service life. The goal is to establish a stronger scientific link between manufacturing and component performance and to contribute to innovative gear design, energy efficient drivetrains, and production excellence.
The postdoctoral researcher will be affiliated with XPRES – Centre of Excellence in Production Research, a long-term national initiative in production research bringing together XPRES KTH, MDU, RISE, and Swerim. As a postdoctoral researcher, you will become part of this dynamic research environment, with opportunities to work across disciplines and in close collaboration with both academia and industry.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Experience in experimental testing (surface fatigue and efficiency tests) using an FZG test rig or an equivalent test machine.
Experience in gear design.
Experience in measuring gear geometry and surface characterisation of gears.
You can communicate scientific results orally and in writing in Swedish and English.
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral researcher position at KTH's Department of Mechanical Design, affiliated with XPRES Centre of Excellence in Production Research. Focus on experimental testing (FZG test rig) of gear performance across manufacturing variations, materials (including powder metallurgy), and lubrication strategies. Interdisciplinary collaboration across mechanical design, materials engineering, and production development.

thematic_fit.rationale: Position is mechanical engineering focused on gear design, manufacturing, and performance testing. Research questions address efficiency, wear, service life, and manufacturing variation—purely technical/mechanical domain. Researcher's domain is human-centered XR, collaborative immersive systems, spatial learning, and wayfinding. Zero thematic overlap. No human interaction, user experience, or immersive systems involved.

methodological_fit.rationale: Position requires experimental testing expertise (FZG test rig, gear geometry characterization, surface analysis) and mechanical design knowledge. Researcher's methodological background is HCI user studies, experimental design for human learning/wayfinding outcomes, and qualitative/quantitative research in immersive systems. Minimal overlap. Both involve experimental design, but applied to entirely different domains and with different analytic goals.

growth_value.rationale: Position offers no capability development relevant to human-centered XR, collaborative immersive systems, spatial cognition, or learning. Would consume 2 years in mechanical engineering with no transfer to target research domain. Does not close any gaps in the researcher's target identity pathway.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is respected; XPRES is a multi-institutional research initiative with industrial collaboration. However, supervisory team focus (mechanical design, materials, production) has no connection to HCI, immersive systems, or user-centered research. Postdoc would build credentials in mechanical engineering only; no pathway to human-centered XR research.
